chunks: He said: Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Basir al-Muqri informed me, saying: Abul Hasan Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Saydalani narrated to us, saying: Abul Miqdam Ahmad ibn Muhammad, the client of Banu Hashim, narrated to us, saying: Abu Nasr al-Makhzumi narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Basri, who said:

When the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, arrived in Basra, he passed by me while I was performing wudu. He said: 'O young man, perform your wudu well, and God will reward you well.' Then he passed me, and I followed in his footsteps. At one point he glanced at me and said: 'O young man, do you need something from me?' I said: 'Yes, teach me words that God may benefit me through.'

He said: 'O young man, whoever is truthful to God is saved; whoever fears for his religion is safe from perdition; and whoever renounces this world, his eyes will be delighted by the reward of God, Mighty and Majestic.'

'Shall I tell you more, young man?' I said: 'Yes indeed, O Commander of the Faithful.' He said: 'Three traits — whoever possesses them, both this world and the hereafter are secure for him: he who enjoins good and follows it himself; forbids evil and refrains from it himself; and safeguards the limits of God. O young man, would it please you to meet God on the Day of Resurrection while He is pleased with you?' I said: 'Yes, O Commander of the Faithful.' He said: 'Be content with little in this world, desirous of the hereafter, and hold fast to truthfulness in all your affairs, for God has ordained you and all His creation to worship through truthfulness.'

Then he walked until he entered the market of Basra. He looked at the people buying and selling, and he wept bitterly, peace be upon him. Then he said: 'O slaves of this world and labourers of its people! If during the day you are busy swearing oaths, and at night you sleep in your beds, and during all that time you are heedless of the hereafter — then when will you prepare provisions and think about the Day of Return?'

A man said to him: 'O Commander of the Faithful, we must earn our livelihood. What should we do?' The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: 'Seeking livelihood through lawful means does not distract from working for the hereafter. But if you say we must hoard and monopolize, you will not be excused.' The man turned away weeping. The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said to him: 'Come to me, I will tell you more.' The man returned to him, and he said: 'Know, O servant of God, that every worker in this world for the hereafter will surely be given his full reward in the hereafter, and every worker who uses his religion for this world — his wages in the hereafter will be the fire of Hell.'

Then the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, recited the words of the Most High: 'As for him who transgressed, and preferred the life of this world, then indeed, the Hellfire will be his abode.' (Quran 79:37-39)

key_terms.الاحتكار: Ihtikaar — hoarding or monopolizing goods; prohibited in Islamic economic ethics as it harms the community
key_terms.الصدق: Al-Sidq — truthfulness/sincerity; presented here as the essential quality God requires in worship and all affairs
key_terms.المعاد: Al-Ma'ad — the Return, referring to the Day of Judgment when all will return to God for reckoning
key_terms.زهد: Zuhd — asceticism, renunciation of worldly attachment; a central concept in Islamic spirituality emphasizing detachment from material excess

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali teach al-Hasan al-Basri about truthfulness, worldly attachment, and earning a livelihood?
ai.summary: This narrative from al-Amali of al-Mufid recounts the famous encounter between Imam Ali (AS) and the young al-Hasan al-Basri in the market of Basra after the Battle of the Camel (36 AH). Imam Ali teaches al-Hasan al-Basri three foundational moral principles — truthfulness before God, concern for one's religion, and renunciation of worldly excess — then proceeds to the marketplace where he admonishes merchants about the balance between earning a livelihood through lawful means and preparing for the hereafter, concluding with a recitation from Surah al-Nazi'at (79:37-39).

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 3. He said: Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Baseer al-Muqri, reported from Abul Hasan ‘Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Saidalani, who reported from Abul Miqdam Ahmad ibn Muhammad, the client of Banu Hashim, who reported from Abu Nasr al-Makhzoomi, from al-Hasan ibn Abu al-Hasan al-Basri who said:

When Amirul Mu’mineen ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, entered Basra, he passed by me while I was doing Wudhoo. He said: "O Young man, do your Wudhoo well, so that Allah may reward you best." Then he proceeded and I followed his wake. At one time, his attention was diverted to me so he asked: "Young man, do you need anything from me?" I said: "Yes, teach me a word of wisdom, so that Allah may grant me its benefit."

He said: "Whoever confirms Allah’s Truth is saved; and whoever fears Him in matters of his faith, is secured from being punished. And whoever contents himself with the least of this world, his eyes will be delighted to behold the rewards of Allah, Most High."

’May I tell you more, young man?" I said: "Yes O, Amirul Mu’mineen." He said: "Whoever has three traits, his fate is secured here and hereafter. He who enjoins good and also follows it; forbids evil and also refrains from it, and does not transgress the limits ordained by Allah. O, young man! Does it please you to meet your Maker, when He is pleased with you?" I said: "Of course, yes, O Amirul Mu’mineen!" He said: "In this world, be content with the least and be desirous of the next world. And you must be truthful in all your affairs, for Allah has ordained for you and all that He has created to worship Him by Truth."

Then he walked away, till he entered the market of Basra. And he saw people busily engaged in buying and selling. He cried bitterly and then proclaimed: "O, slaves of this world! O, labourers of its people! If you remain busy swearing during the day time and sleeping in your beds during the night; and during that time you are totally oblivious to the next world, then when will you prepare the provision (for the journey to the next world) and think about the Day of Return (unto Allah)?"

So, one of them said: "O Amirul Mu’mineen! We have to work for our living. What else should we do?" Amirul Mu’mineen said: "To seek one’s living by legitimate ways does not make you heedless of the next world! But if you say: We must hoard and monopolize, then you cannot be excused." The man turned his face weeping. Amirul Mu’mineen, peace be upon him, told him to come closer so that he would tell him more. He came forth, so ‘Ali, peace be upon him, said: "O servant of Allah! Indeed, everyone who works here for the hereafter will be amply rewarded in the next world. And he who uses his other worldliness for earning this world, he will earn hell fire in exchange."
Then Amirul Mu’mineen recited the following verses: ’Then as for him who was insolent; And preferred the life of this world; Surely, Hell shall be the abode for him.’(al-Naziaat, 79: 37-39)
